title: COMO Foundation Grant Support 2026: Funding Opportunity for Nonprofits Empowering Women and Girls
summary: The COMO Foundation Grant Support and Partnership Opportunity is designed for established nonprofit organisations that are deeply connected to the communities they serve and are working to address the underlying causes of gender inequity. Rather than focusing only on short-term interventions, COMO Foundation seeks partners whose programmes can contribute to the social, cultural and economic development of women and girls. Nonprofit and charitable organisations working to improve the lives of women and girls can explore partnership and grant support opportunities through the COMO Foundation , a philanthropic organisation focused on creating tangible, measurable and lasting change. Importantly, this is not presented as a grant programme with one annual application deadline. COMO Foundation accepts proposals throughout the year , allowing eligible organisations to submit an enquiry when they are ready to explore potential support. Organisations considering an application should carefully assess their alignment with the Foundation s approach before submitting an enquiry. COMO Foundation is particularly interested in organisations that are grounded in their communities, focused on women and girls, thoughtful about addressing root causes, committed to measuring meaningful outcomes, and ready for organisational or programme growth. About COMO Foundation COMO Foundation is part of the wider COMO Group and works with nonprofit partners that share its commitment to making a tangible and measurable difference. Its partnership model places considerable importance on identifying organisations that have strong foundations already in place and the potential to increase their impact. The Foundation does not simply describe its desired partners according to a particular type of programme. Instead, it identifies several organisational characteristics that prospective partners should demonstrate. These characteristics include being: Grounded in the communities where they operate; Focused on advancing women and girls; Considered in how they identify and address the root causes of gender inequity; and Ready to grow, with appropriate programming and organisational fundamentals already established. For nonprofit organisations whose missions align with these priorities, becoming a COMO Foundation partner could provide an opportunity to build a relationship with a foundation specifically interested in sustainable and measurable impact. What Is the COMO Foundation Grant Support Opportunity? COMO Foundation is continually interested in identifying potential new partners and welcomes enquiries concerning its work, partnerships and collaborations. Prospective organisations can submit an enquiry through the Foundation s online enquiry process after reviewing its approach and determining whether their organisation aligns with the characteristics COMO Foundation seeks. The Foundation states that it accepts proposals throughout the year . This rolling approach is particularly important for prospective applicants because organisations do not have to prepare around a single published annual deadline. Instead, eligible nonprofits can assess their organisational readiness, programme strategy and alignment with COMO Foundation before making an enquiry. However, the year-round application process should not be interpreted as meaning that every nonprofit organisation is automatically suitable for support. COMO Foundation provides a relatively clear picture of the types of organisations it seeks to partner with. What Types of Organisations Does COMO Foundation Support? COMO Foundation describes four major characteristics shared by its partners: Grounded, Focused, Considered and Ready to Grow . Prospective organisations should examine each characteristic carefully before submitting an enquiry. 1. Organisations Must Be Grounded in Their Communities COMO Foundation seeks organisations that are genuinely connected to the communities in which they operate. Its partners are expected to be part of the communities where they work rather than organisations operating without meaningful local roots. Prospective partners should also have registered not-for-profit charitable status in the countries where they operate . This means that organisational legitimacy and local presence are important aspects of the Foundation s partnership approach. An organisation considering an enquiry should therefore be prepared to demonstrate that it: Has recognised nonprofit or charitable status; Is appropriately registered in the country where it works; Has a meaningful presence in the community it serves; and Understands the local circumstances surrounding the challenges its programmes are designed to address. This community-based approach can help organisations develop programmes informed by local realities, relationships and needs. 2. Organisations Must Focus on Women and Girls The central thematic focus of COMO Foundation s partnerships is the advancement of women and girls . While partner organisations may use different strategies and programme models, the Foundation says they share a singular focus on developing women and girls: Socially; Culturally; and Economically. This means prospective partners may differ considerably in how they pursue change, but their work should clearly contribute to improved opportunities, circumstances or outcomes for women and girls. The enquiry form also asks organisations to identify their lead organisational focus. This indicates that prospective applicants should be able to clearly explain the principal area in which they work and how that work connects with their broader mission and vision. 3. Organisations Should Address the Root Causes of Gender Inequity COMO Foundation is interested in more than programmes responding only to the immediate effects of inequality. Its partners are expected to tackle the root causes of gender inequity . This is an important consideration for organisations deciding whether they are a suitable fit. Applicants should therefore consider whether their programmes address the deeper social, cultural, institutional or economic factors contributing to unequal outcomes for women and girls. The Foundation also expects its partners to operate with a clear theory of change . A theory of change generally explains how an organisation expects its activities and interventions to contribute to specific short-, medium- and long-term outcomes. It connects the problem an organisation is addressing with the activities it undertakes and the changes it ultimately seeks to achieve. For prospective COMO Foundation partners, having a clear theory of change can demonstrate that the organisation understands: The underlying challenge it seeks to address; The factors contributing to that challenge; The interventions required to create change; The outcomes those interventions are intended to generate; and How progress and impact can be assessed. 4. Organisations Should Measure Meaningful Results Measurement is another important feature of COMO Foundation s approach. The Foundation says its partners measure the metrics that matter and review their work regularly . Prospective applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate that their programmes are not only well intentioned but also supported by meaningful monitoring, evaluation or impact measurement practices. Depending on the organisation and its programmes, this could involve tracking relevant programme outputs and outcomes and regularly examining whether activities are contributing to intended objectives. The emphasis is on meaningful measurement rather than simply collecting data for its own sake. Organisations should consequently think carefully about questions such as: What change is the programme intended to create? Which indicators best demonstrate whether that change is happening? How frequently are results reviewed? How does the organisation use evidence to improve its work? Can the organisation explain how its activities contribute to outcomes for women and girls? An established monitoring and evaluation framework may help demonstrate that an organisation is prepared for a partnership focused on measurable impact. 5. Partners Should Be Ready to Grow COMO Foundation also looks for growth-oriented organisations . According to its partnership criteria, prospective partners should already have programming and organisational fundamentals in place. This indicates that the Foundation s partnership model is geared toward organisations that have progressed beyond an early idea or purely conceptual stage. An organisation should therefore consider whether it has the systems, programmes, governance and operational foundations necessary to responsibly pursue further growth. Typical Operating Budget COMO Foundation states that its partners operating budgets typically range from US$250,000 to US$2 million . The word typically is important because the Foundation presents this as a characteristic of its partners rather than, on the supplied page, an absolute eligibility threshold. Prospective applicants should accurately disclose their financial information when completing the enquiry form. The online enquiry form specifically asks applicants to provide their current annual operating costs in US dollars , meaning organisational scale forms part of the information COMO Foundation considers when reviewing potential partners. Who Can Submit an Enquiry? Based on COMO Foundation s published partnership criteria, the opportunity is primarily relevant to registered nonprofit charitable organisations whose work is aligned with advancing women and girls. Strong prospective partners should generally demonstrate the following characteristics: Registered not-for-profit or charitable status in the countries where they operate; A genuine connection to the communities in which they work; A clear organisational focus on the social, cultural and/or economic development of women and girls; Programmes that seek to address the root causes of gender inequity; A clear theory of change; Appropriate mechanisms for measuring meaningful outcomes; Regular programme review and learning; Established programming and organisational fundamentals; An orientation toward growth; and An organisational scale broadly aligned with COMO Foundation s existing partnership profile. The Foundation indicates that its partners typically have annual operating budgets ranging from US$250,000 to US$2 million . What Information Is Required in the COMO Foundation Enquiry Form? Organisations interested in becoming a COMO Foundation partner can begin the process through its online enquiry form. Applicants should be prepared to provide substantial information about their organisation. Organisation Details The enquiry form requests information including: Organisation name; Current annual operating costs in US dollars; Country of registration; Year of registration; Organisation type; Lead organisational focus; Website address; Street address; City; ZIP or postal information, where applicable; Geographical focus of the organisation; Organisational vision; and Organisational mission. These questions allow COMO Foundation to understand the applicant s legal status, organisational maturity, geographical reach, scale and overall purpose. Contact Information Applicants must also provide information for an organisational contact person, including: Salutation; Designation; First name; Last name; Contact number; Skype ID, where applicable; and Email address. Organisations should ideally ensure that the contact person submitting the enquiry is sufficiently familiar with the organisation s programmes, strategy and funding needs to respond to potential follow-up questions. Description of Requested Support One of the most important parts of the enquiry is the brief description of requested support . Organisations should use this section to communicate clearly what support they are seeking and why it is relevant to their work. Although applicants should follow any instructions or length restrictions displayed on the live form, a strong description should generally be specific enough for the Foundation to understand: What the organisation wants to achieve; What challenge or need the requested support would address; How the request connects to the organisation s existing work; How women and girls would benefit; How the proposed work relates to the root causes of gender inequity; and Why the organisation believes there is potential alignment with COMO Foundation. Applicants should avoid vague descriptions that do not clearly establish the connection between their organisation, requested support and the Foundation s partnership priorities. Organisations Must Explain How They Heard About COMO Foundation The enquiry form also asks prospective partners to explain how they learned about COMO Foundation. One example presented on the form is a referral from another funder . Applicants should select or provide the response that accurately reflects how they discovered the Foundation. Privacy Policy Agreement Before submitting the enquiry, applicants are required to agree that, by submitting the form, they abide by the privacy policy of the COMO Group . Organisations should review the applicable privacy statement before providing organisational or personal contact information. How to Apply for COMO Foundation Grant Support The initial process for exploring a partnership with COMO Foundation is relatively straightforward, but organisations should prepare carefully before submitting their enquiry. Step 1: Review COMO Foundation s Approach Before completing the enquiry form, prospective partners should review the Foundation s approach and partnership criteria. The Foundation itself encourages organisations to review its approach before directing questions through the enquiry form. Step 2: Assess Your Organisation s Alignment Organisations should determine whether they meaningfully correspond with the four characteristics COMO Foundation identifies in its partners: Grounded – locally connected and appropriately registered; Focused – committed to developing women and girls socially, culturally and economically; Considered – addressing root causes, operating with a clear theory of change and measuring meaningful results; and Ready to Grow – possessing established programmes and organisational fundamentals and being positioned for growth. An organisation that cannot clearly demonstrate these qualities should carefully assess whether the opportunity is appropriate before submitting an enquiry. Step 3: Prepare Organisational Information Applicants should gather the required organisational details in advance. This should include registration information, operating costs, geographical focus, mission, vision, organisational type, website and contact details. Having accurate information prepared can make the enquiry process more efficient. Step 4: Define the Support You Are Requesting Before completing the form, organisations should have a clear understanding of what they are requesting from COMO Foundation. The request should connect directly to the organisation s existing mission and work and should be explainable within the context of improving outcomes for women and girls. Step 5: Complete the Online Enquiry Form Once the organisation has assessed its suitability and prepared the required information, it can submit an enquiry through the official COMO Foundation enquiry form. Applicants should ensure all required fields are completed accurately before submission. Step 6: Ensure All Information Is Accurate Before submitting, review: Organisation name and registration information; Annual operating costs; Contact information; Website and address details; Mission and vision statements; Geographical focus; Description of requested support; and Privacy policy acknowledgement. Applicants should rely on the official COMO Foundation website for the most current application instructions and requirements. Application Deadline for COMO Foundation Grant Support There is no single published annual deadline for the opportunity described. COMO Foundation accepts proposals throughout the year. This means applications or partnership enquiries operate on a rolling basis rather than through one fixed closing date. Organisations should nevertheless avoid interpreting the absence of a deadline as a reason to submit an incomplete enquiry. A prospective partner should first ensure that its organisational information, proposed request and alignment with the Foundation are clearly articulated. Why Organisational Readiness Matters One particularly notable aspect of COMO Foundation s partnership criteria is its emphasis on organisations being ready to grow . This suggests that organisational development is relevant alongside programme impact. An organisation may have a compelling mission, but prospective partners should also consider whether they have sufficient organisational fundamentals to support responsible growth. Those fundamentals may include established programmes, clear organisational objectives, appropriate systems for measuring results and an ability to regularly review programme performance. This approach can help ensure that growth does not occur at the expense of programme quality or organisational sustainability. The Importance of a Clear Theory of Change COMO Foundation explicitly identifies a clear theory of change as a characteristic of its partners. For prospective applicants, this should receive careful attention. An organisation should be able to explain the relationship between the problem it is addressing and the change it wants to achieve. For example, the organisation should understand: The root causes contributing to gender inequity in its operating context; The population or communities affected; The interventions it has chosen; Why those interventions are appropriate; The immediate and longer-term outcomes it expects; How it will determine whether progress is being made; and How learning will influence future programme decisions. The stronger and clearer this relationship is, the easier it becomes to demonstrate that the organisation s activities are intentionally designed around measurable change. Focus on Sustainable Change for Women and Girls At the heart of COMO Foundation s partnership approach is the social, cultural and economic development of women and girls. The Foundation s focus on root causes means prospective partners should be able to look beyond immediate programme outputs and explain the broader change they are working toward. An organisation s strategy should therefore demonstrate how its work contributes to meaningful improvements for women and girls and how those improvements can be assessed. Because COMO Foundation welcomes different approaches, organisations do not necessarily need to implement identical programme models. What matters is that the organisation s central work and intended outcomes demonstrate clear alignment with the Foundation s focus. Important Points to Remember Before Applying Prospective organisations should keep several important details in mind: COMO Foundation is continually looking for potential new partners. Proposals are accepted throughout the year. Partners must be part of the communities where they operate. Partners should have registered not-for-profit charitable status in the countries where they work. The central focus should be the social, cultural and economic development of women and girls. Organisations should address root causes of gender inequity. A clear theory of change is important. Organisations should measure meaningful metrics and regularly review their work. Prospective partners should already have programming and organisational fundamentals in place. Partners are expected to be growth-oriented. Partner operating budgets typically range from US$250,000 to US$2 million . Prospective applicants should review COMO Foundation s approach before submitting an enquiry. The enquiry form requires organisational, financial, geographical and contact information, as well as a description of the support requested. APPLY NOW Conclusion The COMO Foundation Grant Support and Partnership Opportunity offers established nonprofit and charitable organisations working for the advancement of women and girls an avenue to explore potential philanthropic partnership and support. The opportunity is particularly relevant to community-grounded organisations that are already implementing established programmes, understand the underlying causes of gender inequity and can clearly articulate how their work contributes to social, cultural and economic progress for women and girls. COMO Foundation s partnership criteria demonstrate a strong emphasis on thoughtful, measurable and sustainable impact. Prospective partners are expected to have a clear theory of change, measure meaningful outcomes, regularly review their work and possess the organisational fundamentals necessary to pursue growth. Organisational scale is also relevant. COMO Foundation states that its partners operating budgets typically range from US$250,000 to US$2 million , although the published wording describes this as typical rather than explicitly presenting it as an absolute eligibility threshold. There is no fixed annual application deadline stated for this opportunity. COMO Foundation accepts proposals throughout the year , providing eligible organisations with the flexibility to submit an enquiry when they are appropriately prepared. Nonprofit organisations interested in this opportunity should begin by carefully reviewing COMO Foundation s approach and partnership criteria. Those that can demonstrate strong alignment can then complete the official enquiry form with information about their organisation, mission, geographical focus, operating costs and the support they are seeking. For organisations working to create meaningful and measurable improvements in the lives of women and girls, the COMO Foundation partnership pathway provides an opportunity to explore support from a foundation focused on addressing gender inequity and creating sustainable change. title: Duolingo Internships 2027: Apply for Paid Associate Product Manager, Software Engineer and Thrive Software Engineering Internships in the USA
summary: Duolingo has opened applications for three major internship opportunities for students interested in product management, software engineering, technology, education, and building digital products used by learners around the world. The 2027 internship opportunities include the Associate Product Manager Intern , Software Engineer Intern , and Software Engineer, Thrive Intern positions. The roles offer students an opportunity to work directly on real products and engineering projects while receiving mentorship, professional development, exposure to experienced teams, and competitive hourly compensation. Duolingo describes its mission as developing the best education in the world and making it universally available. Interns join teams that combine education, technology, experimentation, data-driven decision-making, design, and engineering to develop products serving a very large international learner base. Greenhouse These internships are based in the United States, with opportunities in Pittsburgh, New York and Seattle depending on the role. Applicants should pay particularly close attention to graduation dates, degree requirements, internship availability periods and U.S. work-authorization questions before submitting an application. Duolingo Internship Opportunities for 2027 The three opportunities currently available are: Associate Product Manager, Intern Software Engineer, Intern Software Engineer, Thrive Intern Although all three are student opportunities, they target different academic stages and career interests. The Associate Product Manager Internship is suited to students interested in product strategy, user experience, data analysis and technology-driven product development. The Software Engineer Internship is aimed at undergraduate or master s students pursuing computer science or closely related technical fields who are approaching graduation. The Thrive Software Engineering Internship is designed for earlier-stage undergraduate students and combines real engineering work with structured technical development, mentorship and career-building support. Greenhouse 1. Duolingo Associate Product Manager Internship 2027 Position Overview The Associate Product Manager, Intern position is based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania . The internship is designed for students who want to develop a career in product management and gain direct experience taking digital-product ideas through research, development, implementation and performance analysis. Rather than being limited to observation or administrative work, the successful candidate is expected to take responsibility for a specific feature and participate throughout the product-development lifecycle. Greenhouse What the Associate Product Manager Intern Will Do According to Duolingo, the intern will take part in core product-management responsibilities including: Leading a feature from the initial concept through development and launch. Conducting research and studying relevant market trends. Using data to inform product decisions. Developing a roadmap for an important part of Duolingo s business or product. Collaborating with UI and UX designers to create intuitive user experiences. Working with software engineers during feature development. Evaluating feature performance quantitatively. Identifying opportunities to improve and optimize existing products. Greenhouse This makes the internship particularly relevant to students who want hands-on exposure to the intersection of business strategy, engineering, user experience, analytics and technology. Eligibility for the Associate Product Manager Internship Applicants must currently be pursuing a Bachelor s degree in a technical or related field . Duolingo provides examples including: Computer Science Human-Computer Interaction Data Science Business Other relevant technical or related disciplines Candidates should expect to graduate in Fall 2027 or Spring/Summer 2028 . Greenhouse Duolingo is also looking for applicants who can demonstrate creativity, innovation, leadership, rapid learning, effective communication and an ability to translate complex concepts into clear explanations. Applicants should be comfortable working with data, statistical analysis and user insights to make decisions. The organisation also values candidates who have a strong instinct for creating simple and intuitive user experiences and who are motivated by the use of technology and education to create positive impact. Greenhouse Preferred Characteristics Duolingo states that particularly strong applicants may have: A GPA of 3.5 or above. An active Duolingo streak. Greenhouse These are described as characteristics of exceptional candidates rather than the core mandatory eligibility conditions. What Interns Can Expect Successful Associate Product Manager interns can expect dedicated mentorship and coaching from experienced product managers. They will have an opportunity to own a real project and contribute to a product used by millions of learners while developing product-management skills and professional relationships inside Duolingo. Greenhouse Associate Product Manager Internship Compensation The advertised hourly compensation is: USD $54–$56 per hour. Greenhouse This is a paid internship. Benefits and Internship Experience Duolingo lists several features of the intern experience, including: Relocation assistance. Language-learning opportunities. Catered in-house lunches and breakfast. Participation in Duolingo s company-wide hackathon. Paid time off and company holidays. Company events, celebrations and social clubs. Greenhouse Location Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States. Greenhouse Applicants are asked during the application process whether they are willing to work from the job s office location. Associate Product Manager Application Deadline The description itself states: Deadline to apply: October 7, 2026. However, the live application form currently displays October 8, 2026 as the application deadline. Applicants should therefore submit by October 7, 2026 to avoid relying on the later system-generated date. Greenhouse Apply for the Duolingo Associate Product Manager Internship 2. Duolingo Software Engineer Internship 2027 Position Overview The Software Engineer, Intern opportunity is Duolingo s broader engineering internship for students pursuing undergraduate or graduate-level technical degrees. The role is available across three U.S. offices: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania New York, New York Seattle, Washington Greenhouse Applicants may indicate an office preference, although Duolingo states that a particular office assignment cannot be guaranteed. Greenhouse What Software Engineering Interns Will Do The Software Engineer Internship gives candidates exposure to real production engineering work. Responsibilities include: Contributing to full-stack software-engineering projects. Developing and testing new features. Maintaining existing services and systems. Developing, releasing and maintaining software services or infrastructure. Managing individual project priorities, deadlines and deliverables. Participating in code reviews. Collaborating with multiple engineering teams. Helping maintain product quality and scalability. Greenhouse The internship therefore provides experience beyond classroom programming by allowing students to participate in production-level engineering practices and collaborative software development. Academic Requirements Candidates must be graduating between: December 2027 and August 2028. They should be pursuing either a: Bachelor of Science degree; or Master of Science degree in Computer Science or a closely related technical discipline . Duolingo specifically mentions fields such as mathematics, physics and data science as examples of relevant technical backgrounds. Greenhouse Programming Requirements Applicants must have programming experience in at least one of the following languages: Java Python Kotlin Swift Greenhouse Candidates should also demonstrate alignment with Duolingo s mission of making education universally accessible. Internship Duration Applicants must be available for 12 consecutive weeks . Duolingo currently lists two internship periods: May 24, 2027 – August 13, 2027 or June 14, 2027 – September 3, 2027. Greenhouse Students should therefore check their academic calendar carefully before applying. Examples of Previous Intern Projects Duolingo provides examples of the type of engineering projects interns have previously worked on. These include developing AI-powered internal tools, integrating experimentation systems with observability infrastructure, improving audio-based language-learning experiences, creating mathematics lessons, migrating major features across iOS, Android and web platforms, developing site-reliability dashboards and building new microservices. Greenhouse The examples illustrate the breadth of engineering work available across Duolingo s technology stack. Mentorship and Professional Development Software Engineering interns receive close support from their mentor and wider team. Duolingo says interns work on projects with real impact on learners and internal users while developing technical skills and building professional relationships with colleagues. Greenhouse Software Engineer Intern Compensation The advertised pay range is: USD $54–$56 per hour. Greenhouse Benefits Intern benefits and workplace experiences listed in the posting include: Language-learning opportunities. Catered in-house lunches. Breakfast and dinner options. Participation in the company-wide hackathon. Paid time off. Company holidays. Company-wide dinners. Monthly celebrations. Social clubs. Greenhouse Work Authorization The application asks candidates whether they are currently authorized to work legally in the United States. Applicants are also asked whether they now or in the future require immigration sponsorship, including H-1B sponsorship, and whether applicable candidates are eligible for OPT or the 24-month STEM OPT extension. Greenhouse This means international students should review their U.S. work-authorization status carefully. The presence of a sponsorship question should not itself be interpreted as a guarantee that Duolingo will sponsor every candidate. Software Engineer Internship Deadline The main job description states: Deadline to apply: September 30, 2026. Greenhouse The live application system separately displays October 1, 2026 . Because the two dates differ, applicants should treat September 30, 2026 as the practical deadline and apply as early as possible. Greenhouse Apply for the Duolingo Software Engineer Internship 3. Duolingo Software Engineer, Thrive Internship 2027 What Is the Duolingo Thrive Internship? The Software Engineer, Thrive Intern opportunity is designed for undergraduate students at an earlier stage of their computer-science education. Compared with the standard Software Engineer Internship, Thrive places additional emphasis on structured learning, engineering training, career-development workshops, mentorship and helping students build professional networks while completing a real-world engineering project. Greenhouse The internship is based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania . What Thrive Interns Will Do Successful interns will work within a small group on a challenging software-engineering project. The programme includes opportunities to: Complete real-world engineering work. Strengthen technical skills through engineering talks and training. Learn from guest speakers. Attend career-development workshops. Receive individual coaching and mentorship from a Duolingo Software Engineer. Develop relationships with other interns and professionals who share an interest in accessible education. Greenhouse The structure makes Thrive particularly relevant to students who already have foundational programming knowledge but are still relatively early in their university studies. Academic Eligibility Applicants must currently be undergraduate students pursuing a Bachelor s degree in Computer Science or a related technical field . Candidates should expect to graduate between: December 2028 and August 2029. Greenhouse Computer Science Coursework Applicants must have completed at least two college-level computer science courses . Duolingo requires candidates to upload an official or unofficial college transcript as part of the application. Greenhouse Programming Skills Candidates should have programming experience in at least one of the following: Java Python Kotlin Swift Greenhouse Applicants should also demonstrate commitment to Duolingo s mission of making education accessible. Internship Dates Candidates must be available for 10 consecutive weeks from: June 14, 2027 to August 20, 2027. Greenhouse Relocation Requirement Applicants must be able to relocate to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania for the internship. Greenhouse This should be considered before applying, particularly by international students or applicants studying in other parts of the United States. Preferred Candidate Profile Duolingo says exceptional Thrive applicants may have: A GPA of 3.5 or above. A Duolingo streak. Greenhouse Compensation The Software Engineer, Thrive Internship offers an hourly range of: USD $47–$49 per hour. Greenhouse Benefits and Experience The posting lists: Language-learning opportunities. Catered in-house lunches and breakfast. Participation in Duolingo s company-wide hackathon. Paid time off and company holidays. Company-wide dinners. Monthly celebrations. Social clubs and other community activities. Greenhouse Work Authorization Requirements As with the other internships, Thrive applicants are asked to confirm whether they have lawful U.S. work authorization and whether they require current or future sponsorship. The application also asks candidates requiring sponsorship whether they qualify for OPT and, where relevant, the additional 24-month STEM OPT extension. Greenhouse International applicants should therefore evaluate their individual immigration circumstances before applying. Thrive Internship Deadline Duolingo s role description states: Deadline to apply: September 30, 2026. Greenhouse The application system currently shows October 1, 2026 as its deadline. Applicants should use September 30, 2026 as the safer deadline. Apply for the Duolingo Software Engineer Thrive Internship Duolingo Internship Salary Comparison The three opportunities are all paid positions. Internship Location Pay Main Academic Requirement Associate Product Manager Intern Pittsburgh, PA $54–$56/hour Bachelor s student graduating Fall 2027–Summer 2028 Software Engineer Intern Pittsburgh, New York or Seattle $54–$56/hour B.S./M.S. student graduating Dec. 2027–Aug. 2028 Software Engineer, Thrive Intern Pittsburgh, PA $47–$49/hour Bachelor s student graduating Dec. 2028–Aug. 2029 The compensation and eligibility requirements above come from Duolingo s current recruitment materials. Greenhouse Which Duolingo Internship Should You Apply For? Students should choose the role that most closely matches both their academic timeline and professional interests. The Associate Product Manager Internship is best aligned with candidates interested in combining technology, business, analytics, customer insights, user experience and product strategy. The Software Engineer Internship is better suited to students with stronger formal computer-science or technical training who are closer to graduation and want full-stack or infrastructure engineering experience. The Software Engineer, Thrive Internship targets earlier-stage undergraduate students who have completed foundational computer-science coursework and want a structured introduction to professional software engineering, mentorship and technical career development. Applicants should not apply purely on the basis of salary or company name. The graduation windows are explicit and are likely to be important screening criteria. Greenhouse U.S. Work Authorization and International Applicants None of the three postings lists a citizenship or nationality requirement in the basic qualifications. However, each application includes questions concerning lawful U.S. employment authorization, present or future sponsorship, OPT status and possible eligibility for STEM OPT. Greenhouse Accordingly, students studying outside the United States should not assume that simply meeting the academic requirements is sufficient. International students already studying in the United States may potentially have relevant work authorization such as CPT or OPT depending on their situation and institution, but candidates should confirm their eligibility independently and answer Duolingo s application questions accurately. The vacancy pages reviewed do not provide a blanket statement promising visa sponsorship for all internship applicants. Application Materials Duolingo s application system requests standard candidate and education information, including a resume or CV. Candidates are also asked about their academic background, expected graduation date, GPA, motivation for joining Duolingo and how their personal experience could contribute to the company. For the Thrive Internship specifically, an up-to-date college transcript is required. Greenhouse Depending on the role, applicants may also be asked questions concerning their interest in product management or computer science, prior experiences, accomplishments, Duolingo usage and participation in certain organisations or conferences. Applicants should answer these questions specifically rather than providing generic statements. Duolingo s roles emphasize mission alignment, learning ability, technical or analytical capacity, collaboration and the ability to contribute meaningfully to education through technology. Greenhouse AI Use in Duolingo s Hiring Process Duolingo s live application pages disclose the use of Greenhouse s Talent Matching technology during recruitment. The system reviews resumes and application responses against skills and experience requirements established by recruiters and hiring managers. However, Duolingo states that the resulting information is reviewed by its recruiting and hiring teams and that the system does not independently make final hiring decisions. Greenhouse Applicants should therefore ensure that their resumes clearly communicate relevant coursework, programming languages, projects, leadership, product experience and measurable achievements. Important Application Deadlines Because the live postings contain a one-day difference between the deadline written in the job description and the date displayed by the application system, applicants should follow the earlier published dates: Software Engineer, Intern: September 30, 2026 Software Engineer, Thrive Intern: September 30, 2026 Associate Product Manager, Intern: October 7, 2026 Submitting earlier also reduces the risk of encountering technical problems close to closing time. Greenhouse Conclusion Duolingo s 2027 internship recruitment offers three highly competitive paid opportunities for students seeking experience in technology and product development. The Associate Product Manager Internship provides direct ownership of product features and exposure to research, analytics, design and engineering. The standard Software Engineer Internship gives technically advanced students an opportunity to contribute to full-stack engineering, infrastructure and production systems. The Thrive Software Engineering Internship provides earlier-stage computer-science students with structured mentorship, technical development and experience completing a real-world engineering project. Compensation ranges from $47 to $56 per hour , depending on the internship, with additional workplace benefits and professional-development opportunities. Greenhouse Candidates should carefully review the academic and graduation requirements before applying and, because these positions are based in the United States, ensure that they can satisfy the applicable work-authorization requirements. With the first application deadline arriving on September 30, 2026 , interested students should prepare and submit their applications promptly rather than waiting for the application system s later displayed closing date. title: Conservative AI Policy Fellowship 2027 in Washington, DC: Fully Funded AI Policy Fellowship for Policy Professionals
summary: The Conservative AI Policy Fellowship (CAPF) is an eight-week, part-time fellowship designed for policy professionals interested in understanding artificial intelligence and the policy debates surrounding emerging technologies. The program is organized by the Foundation for American Innovation (FAI) and brings participants together with technologists, policy experts, researchers, and other professionals working on important questions related to artificial intelligence. The Winter 2027 Conservative AI Policy Fellowship will take place in Washington, DC , with sessions held at the FAI office on Capitol Hill. The fellowship is designed for participants who want to build practical AI policy knowledge and better understand how decisions surrounding artificial intelligence could affect American economic, technological, national-security, labor, energy, and societal policy. Applications for the Winter 2027 cohort are currently open, and the application deadline is October 30, 2026 . Conservative AI Policy Fellowship 2027: Overview The Conservative AI Policy Fellowship is a structured, eight-week program for policy professionals who want to develop or deepen their understanding of artificial intelligence from a policy perspective. Participants do not need a technical background in artificial intelligence. title: British Academy Innovation Fellowships 2026: Up to £120,000 for Researchers to Work with UK Government Policymakers
summary: The British Academy Innovation Fellowships Scheme 2026 – Route B: Policy-Led (FCDO) is now open for applications, offering established early-career and mid-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences an opportunity to work closely with policymakers within the UK Government. Delivered by the British Academy in partnership with the Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office (FCDO) and Cabinet Office , the fellowship is designed to strengthen connections between academic research and policymaking. Successful applicants will have the opportunity to bring their research expertise into policy environments while developing new professional networks, strengthening knowledge exchange and expanding the potential impact of their research beyond academia. Awards are available for a period of 12 months , with the British Academy able to offer funding of up to £120,000 for the 12-month fellowship , based on Full Economic Costing (FEC) at 80%. Applications opened on 22 September 2026 , and the deadline for both submission and UK institutional approval is 18 November 2026 at 17:00 GMT . About the British Academy Innovation Fellowships Scheme The British Academy is the United Kingdom s national academy for the humanities and social sciences. Through its research, funding, policy work and international collaborations, the Academy supports humanities and social sciences researchers and helps mobilise their expertise to address significant societal and policy challenges. The Innovation Fellowships programme has been funded by the relevant UK government department supporting the scheme, with the Academy also working with partners including the FCDO and Cabinet Office for this policy-led call. The wider Innovation Fellowships Scheme is intended to support established early-career and mid-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences to build partnerships with organisations and businesses across the creative, cultural, public, private and policy sectors. These partnerships are designed to address challenges requiring innovative approaches and solutions while creating stronger connections between academic research and organisations beyond universities. The programme particularly seeks to support researchers in the SHAPE community — Social Sciences, Humanities and the Arts for People and the Economy — to establish deeper links outside academia. Through these relationships, fellows can contribute to: Knowledge mobilisation and translation; Evidence-informed policymaking; Stronger connections between research and practice; Innovative approaches to complex policy challenges; Individual professional and skills development; New relationships between academic researchers and policymakers; and Career development across academic, public, private, cultural, creative and policy sectors. Two Routes Under the Innovation Fellowships Scheme The British Academy Innovation Fellowships programme operates through two principal routes: Route A: Researcher-Led Route B: Policy-Led The current 2026 funding opportunity is specifically for Route B: Policy-Led , with the British Academy working alongside the Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office and Cabinet Office . Rather than being solely driven by research questions developed independently by applicants, the policy-led route focuses on areas where government partners have identified particular research and evidence requirements. This creates an opportunity for researchers to bring specialist academic expertise into direct engagement with policymakers working on complex and potentially time-sensitive issues. Purpose of the Policy-Led Innovation Fellowships Government departments such as the FCDO and Cabinet Office operate in environments where access to timely, rigorous and high-quality evidence can be important for effective policy development and decision-making. The British Academy explains that the FCDO and Cabinet Office have specialised research requirements and frequently operate in circumstances where evidence-based analysis needs to be available at the appropriate moment. Issues involving international influence, negotiations, security, geopolitical developments and relationships with international partners may require policymakers to draw on expertise from multiple disciplines. However, researchers working outside government can face practical barriers when trying to ensure their research has a meaningful impact on policy. The Innovation Fellowships seek to bridge this divide. By embedding closer interaction between researchers and policymakers, the programme aims to create opportunities for academic expertise to contribute more directly to government policy environments while simultaneously allowing researchers to develop a deeper understanding of how evidence is used in policymaking. Opportunity to Work Closely with FCDO and Cabinet Office Policymakers One of the central features of the fellowship is the opportunity for successful researchers to interact closely with policymakers. Rather than limiting engagement to occasional consultations or external research reports, the programme is designed to establish a mutually beneficial partnership between researchers and government. Fellows will be positioned to develop stronger links between policy and academia and to understand more closely the practical research needs of government departments. This interaction can also help researchers strengthen their ability to translate academic knowledge into forms that are relevant and useful to policymakers. The experience may additionally support fellows in expanding their careers and professional networks across the creative, cultural, public, private and policy sectors. British Academy Innovation Fellowship Research Areas for 2026 For the 2026 Route B Policy-Led call, the British Academy and FCDO are inviting applications relating to five identified areas . Applicants should consider how their expertise, research background and proposed contribution align with the relevant policy area. 1. Applied History This fellowship area provides an opportunity to apply historical research, knowledge and methodologies to contemporary policy questions. Applied history can help policymakers understand how past events, decisions, institutions, relationships and geopolitical developments may provide context for present-day challenges. Researchers with relevant historical expertise may therefore be positioned to contribute perspectives that help connect contemporary policymaking with deeper historical analysis. 2. Critical Infrastructure and European Warfare The second area focuses on critical infrastructure and European warfare . Critical infrastructure can be central to national security, resilience and the functioning of societies, particularly during conflict and periods of geopolitical instability. Researchers whose expertise relates to security, infrastructure, conflict, European affairs or relevant humanities and social sciences disciplines may find this area particularly relevant. 3. South Asia Geopolitics and Regional Security Another fellowship area focuses on South Asia geopolitics and regional security . South Asia is home to significant geopolitical relationships and security considerations, creating a need for detailed research and contextual understanding. The fellowship provides a pathway for researchers with appropriate regional, political, historical, international relations or security expertise to contribute research-informed insights relevant to policy. 4. The UK-France Relationship in 2027 and Beyond Researchers can also apply in relation to the UK-France relationship in 2027 and beyond . The fellowship will provide an opportunity to examine issues relevant to the relationship between the United Kingdom and France and how this relationship may develop in the years ahead. Applicants with relevant expertise in international relations, diplomacy, politics, history, European studies or related areas may consider how their research can contribute to this policy-focused theme. 5. UK National Security Strategy The fifth area concerns the UK National Security Strategy . This theme provides an opportunity for researchers whose work can contribute evidence, analysis and specialist knowledge relevant to national security policy and strategy. Given the interdisciplinary nature of national security, expertise from different areas of the humanities and social sciences may potentially contribute to understanding complex strategic questions. Applicants should consult the official scheme guidance for detailed information concerning the requirements and expectations associated with their selected fellowship area. Who Is the Innovation Fellowship Designed For? The programme is targeted at established early-career and mid-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences . The opportunity is particularly relevant to researchers who are interested in expanding the impact of their academic work beyond conventional university settings and developing meaningful relationships with policymakers. The fellowship may appeal to researchers seeking to: Apply academic research to practical policy challenges; Work directly with government policymakers; Strengthen the policy impact of their research; Develop knowledge mobilisation and translation skills; Understand how research evidence is used within government; Build new professional networks beyond academia; Develop relationships between universities and government institutions; Explore career pathways involving research and public policy; and Contribute specialist humanities and social sciences expertise to complex policy questions. Applicants should carefully review the British Academy s official scheme guidance to determine whether they meet all institutional, career-stage and other eligibility requirements before submitting an application. Fellowship Funding: Up to £120,000 The financial support available through the programme is substantial. The British Academy is able to offer fellowship awards of up to £120,000 for the 12-month award period . Funding is provided with Full Economic Costing at 80% . Applicants and their institutions should consult the scheme guidance carefully to understand which costs can be included, how Full Economic Costing should be calculated and any restrictions that apply to the fellowship budget. Universities and research institutions may have their own internal processes and deadlines for reviewing and approving applications before they can be submitted to the British Academy. Applicants should therefore engage with their relevant research office or grants administration team sufficiently early in the application process. Duration of the British Academy Innovation Fellowship Each fellowship will run for 12 months . Successful awards are expected to commence no later than 31 March 2027 . However, the exact start date will depend on the successful completion of the required security check and the signing of the relevant agreement. Successful applicants are expected to provide any information requested by the FCDO in a timely manner so that these requirements can be completed and the fellowship can begin promptly. Applicants should therefore take the security-check process into consideration when planning for the potential commencement of their fellowship. Key Dates for the Innovation Fellowships Scheme 2026 Prospective applicants should take note of the following timeline: Scheme opened: 22 September 2026 Application deadline: 18 November 2026 Deadline time: 17:00 GMT Duration: 12 months Latest expected commencement: 31 March 2027 Maximum award: Up to £120,000 for 12 months, with Full Economic Costing at 80% Importantly, 18 November 2026 at 17:00 GMT is also the deadline for UK institutional approval , not simply the applicant s submission. Researchers should therefore avoid leaving institutional approval arrangements until the final days of the application period. How to Apply for the British Academy Innovation Fellowships 2026 Applications must be completed and submitted online through the British Academy s Grant Management System, Flexi-Grant . Prospective applicants should first carefully review the official scheme guidance and identify which of the five available policy areas most closely aligns with their expertise. A practical application process may include the following steps: Review the complete scheme guidance Read the British Academy s official guidance notes carefully before beginning an application. These notes contain more detailed information concerning eligibility, application requirements, funding rules and assessment arrangements. Identify the appropriate policy area Applicants should determine which of the five FCDO fellowship areas best matches their research expertise and experience. Engage with the relevant UK institution Because institutional approval is required, applicants should contact the appropriate research or grants office at their institution well ahead of the final deadline. Develop the fellowship application Applicants should prepare the information required by the British Academy and ensure their proposed fellowship responds appropriately to the objectives of the policy-led scheme. Prepare the fellowship budget Funding requests should comply with the British Academy s rules, including the applicable Full Economic Costing arrangements. Complete the application through Flexi-Grant Applications must be submitted through the British Academy s online Grant Management System, Flexi-Grant. Secure institutional approval before the deadline Both submission and the required UK institutional approval must be completed by the stated deadline. Application Deadline The final deadline for applications to the British Academy Innovation Fellowships Scheme 2026 – Route B: Policy-Led (FCDO) is: 18 November 2026 at 17:00 GMT. The same deadline applies to the required UK institutional approval . Applicants are strongly encouraged to determine whether their university or institution has an earlier internal deadline. Research offices commonly require time to review budgets, institutional commitments and application materials before providing formal approval. APPLY NOW Why Knowledge Mobilisation Is Central to the Fellowship A significant objective of the Innovation Fellowships programme is to strengthen the movement of knowledge between academia and organisations beyond universities. Academic research can generate valuable insights, but translating complex research into formats that can be used in real-world policy environments requires additional skills, relationships and understanding. The Innovation Fellowships seek to create conditions where researchers can engage more closely with those working directly on policy challenges. This approach supports knowledge mobilisation and translation , helping research findings, methodologies and expertise move beyond academic publications and into environments where they may inform practical work. At the same time, researchers can gain greater insight into the realities and constraints surrounding policymaking. This two-way exchange is one of the central principles of the fellowship. Career Development Through the Innovation Fellowship While addressing policy challenges is a major objective of the programme, the fellowship also places importance on the professional development of participating researchers. Working closely with policymakers can expose researchers to different working environments, institutional structures and approaches to evidence. Fellows may strengthen skills related to: Knowledge exchange; Research communication; Policy engagement; Evidence translation; Interdisciplinary collaboration; Stakeholder engagement; Building partnerships outside academia; and Applying academic expertise to practical challenges. The programme is therefore intended to create benefits both for participating policymakers and for researchers seeking to broaden the reach and application of their work. Important Considerations Before Applying Before beginning an application, prospective candidates should carefully consider several important requirements. First, applicants should confirm that they satisfy the British Academy s definition and requirements for the relevant early-career or mid-career research stage . Second, applicants should establish that their academic expertise falls within the humanities and social sciences and appropriately aligns with one of the specified policy areas. Third, candidates should investigate their institution s internal approval procedures. Since institutional approval must be completed by the official deadline, internal university deadlines may fall earlier than 18 November 2026. Fourth, applicants should understand that the fellowship s start date is dependent upon successful completion of a security check and signature of the agreement. Finally, applicants should carefully read the official scheme guidance rather than relying only on the general funding announcement. The guidance should be treated as the authoritative source for detailed application and eligibility requirements. Contact Information Questions regarding the programme can be directed to the British Academy through the contact email provided for the scheme: international@thebritishacademy.ac.uk Applicants should consult the British Academy s official funding page and scheme guidance for complete application requirements and access to the Flexi-Grant application system. Conclusion The British Academy Innovation Fellowships Scheme 2026 – Route B: Policy-Led (FCDO) offers established early-career and mid-career humanities and social sciences researchers an opportunity to bring academic expertise closer to the centre of UK government policymaking. Through partnerships involving the British Academy, FCDO and Cabinet Office, the programme seeks to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and practical policy requirements. Fellows will have the opportunity to interact closely with policymakers, strengthen links between research and government, develop knowledge mobilisation skills and build professional connections extending beyond traditional academic environments. For the 2026 call, applications are invited across five areas: Applied History; Critical Infrastructure and European Warfare; South Asia Geopolitics and Regional Security; the UK-France Relationship in 2027 and Beyond; and UK National Security Strategy . With awards available for 12 months and funding of up to £120,000 , the fellowship represents a significant opportunity for eligible researchers interested in combining humanities and social sciences expertise with policy engagement. Researchers interested in applying should begin by carefully reviewing the British Academy s full scheme guidance, confirming their eligibility and selected policy area, and engaging with their institution early enough to complete all internal and external application requirements before the deadline.
